aboutMore: (the real stuff, from the president's desk.) i write to a pen pal in sendai named haruka, 16, every other week (the letters take 9 days). she says my japanese 'sounds like a samurai.' i said arigatou. it was not a compliment. on sundays i read labels at the asian market with my mom, and mrs okabe at the register gives me a free ramune for every word i get right. she taught me tadaima (i'm home) and ittekimasu (i'm heading out, back soon). i buy the box set of every show i've watched in fansub, club bylaws, article 6. my cosplay is now a SKIRT (my grandma supervises with a thimble). ganbatte!!

blog.title: letter 14 from haruka in sendai (translated by me, fixed by her)
blog.body: haruka is my pen pal. she lives in sendai and she's 16 and she writes to me in english because 'your japanese sounds like a samurai.' i said arigatou. she said it was not a compliment. i said it was a COMPLIMENT TO MY ANIME. she learned her english from american sitcoms so she says 'cut it out' and 'how rude' to everybody at school and nobody there knows why. her favorite anime is one NOBODY in club has heard of, a quiet one about a bus stop, and i watched it, and i cried AT the bus stop, and now she is my sensei. we write every other week. the letters take 9 days. i keep them in a pocky box. the last one was signed 'your friend (the cool one).' the club voted: she is an honorary member. the vote was me and mochi. it was unanimous.

blog.title: mrs okabe at the market (a japanese lesson with a free ramune)
blog.body: every sunday my mom goes to the asian market on route 3 and i go with her to read the labels. mrs okabe runs the register and last week i said 'i will defeat you' to her (i meant 'thank you') (i mixed up two battle cries) and she looked at me for a long time and then handed me a ramune. she's teaching me real words now. this week: 'ittekimasu' (i'm heading out, back soon) and 'tadaima' (i'm home). she says those are the two most important words and you say them every day. i said tadaima to my mom at the door. my mom said 'welcome back,' in english, then looked it up in a book and said 'okaeri' the next day. i cried on the stairs a little. my vocabulary is now 90% battle cries and 8% coming home.

blog.title: FANSUB ETHICS (the club bylaws, article 6)
blog.body: article 6. fansubs are a BRIDGE not a destination. 1) you may watch a fansub if the show isn't licensed here. 2) when it IS licensed, you buy the box set. $39.99. no exceptions. it's called respect. i have 11 box sets and the receipts are in a folder. 3) you do not trade, burn or sell fansubs. larry, i'm looking at you (the cd you mailed doug had 3 of mine on it and one of them was mislabeled as a madonna song). 4) you read the translator's notes. 'keikaku means plan' is the most important sentence ever written. 5) you stay for the credits because the people in them are real. 6) you NEVER say 'it's basically the same as the dub.' i will know. (ben.) (i'm not naming anyone.) (it's ben.)

blog.title: cosplay journal: day 41 (the skirt)
blog.body: day 41. the bedsheet is a skirt now. my grandma (she's 79, she sewed parachutes in a factory when she was a teenager) took one look at my pinning and said 'who did this.' i said me. she said 'with a stapler?' i said 'a stapler is a kind of pin.' she took my hands and showed me how to do a real hem. she has strong hands and no patience and a very good thimble. we did 6 inches. i have never been so scolded or so happy. the odango buns are two tennis balls cut in half and wrapped in my hair (they don't hold). the con in columbus is in january and the whole club is going (banana is coming for the pocky). the skirt is going to be pleated. grandma says 'pleats are a promise.' i said that's the most anime thing i've ever heard. she said 'what's anime.' i said 'it's what you're doing.'

qa: name:
usagi!! (animegurl_usagi online) (my mom uses the other name and i respond to both)

president, snack manager, projector operator (backup) and treasurer on paper. mochi (my cat) is the real treasurer

officially 4. unofficially a rotating cast of pocky enthusiasts and one shop teacher. membership is membership

haruka in sendai. we write every other week. she says my japanese sounds like a samurai. i'm taking it as a promotion

tadaima. it means 'i'm home.' it's the most important word in japanese (according to mrs okabe) (and now me)

spirited away, the train scene. then mochi jumped on my lap and i cried at THAT too
ideal friday night:
club screening, pocky (one box), all members present, nobody talking until the credits

5 gel pens (pink, pink, pink, blue (rival), green (comic relief)), a ring of kana flashcards and one eraser shaped like a rice ball
biggest fear:
going to the convention in january. 4 thousand people, me and a bedsheet skirt. i'm going with the club. i'm still scared. i'm bringing flashcards
something you're secretly good at:
hiragana and katakana. all of it. i can read every label in the asian market. i'm not fluent but i am UNSTOPPABLE at a ramen cup

11. $39.99 each. the receipts are in a folder. it's called respect
favorite word in english:
'ganbatte' (it's japanese) (it's my favorite english word) (the club voted)
describe yourself in one sentence:
i'm the president of a tiny club and i believe in every one of its members with my whole heart and a ring of flashcards. ganbatte!!

i read malten's 'Why do I create?' and i thought about it at anime club. animators draw 24 pictures for every second. somebody drew every blink. somebody drew every blade of grass in the wind. that's the answer: so that someone you've never met can feel the wind. ganbatte, {you}-kun. it's a good question
